exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated management endpoints are directly exploitable public-facing attack surfaces.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Active Scanning
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers actively scan for exposed management endpoints to identify unauthenticated access points.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Without TLS enforcement, plaintext traffic on inbound connections is vulnerable to interception via network sniffing.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Downgrade Attack
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or default TLS configurations enable downgrade attacks that force use of weaker cipher suites or protocol versions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Default or misconfigured TLS settings directly weaken encryption strength, aligning with this technique.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
exploitedBy.relevance: Processes with excessive OS privileges provide an elevated foothold that attackers exploit to escalate privileges further.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Secrets stored in plaintext on disk are directly targeted by credential harvesting from files.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext secrets in environment variables or disk represent unsecured credentials that adversaries search for.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing or incomplete logging is analogous to disabled/modified logs, preventing detection of malicious activity.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Indicator Blocking
exploitedBy.relevance: Incomplete logging results in blocking of indicators that would otherwise surface attacker activity.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Log Enumeration
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers enumerate logs to harvest sensitive data that has leaked into log output.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Sensitive data leaked in logs often includes credentials that adversaries collect for reconnaissance or access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Known vulnerabilities in unpatched runtimes are exploited to compromise remote services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Service Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Services bound to all interfaces are more easily discovered by adversaries scanning for network services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Overly permissive network binding can bridge internal and external network boundaries, enabling lateral movement.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rate limiting, applications are vulnerable to exhaustion floods that overwhelm application-layer resources.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing throttling allows service exhaustion attacks that degrade or deny service availability.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol or Service Impersonation
exploitedBy.relevance: Without mutual TLS, services cannot verify peer identity, enabling impersonation of legitimate services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of mTLS allows attackers to intercept or tunnel through inter-service communication undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Forge Web Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: JWT validation misconfigurations allow attackers to forge or manipulate web tokens to gain unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
exploitedBy.relevance: Misconfigured token validation enables use of crafted or stolen tokens as alternate authentication material.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Fallback Channels
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of circuit breaker configuration leaves no controlled fallback, mirroring the resilience gap exploited by fallback channel techniques.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Server Software Component
exploitedBy.relevance: Debug mode in production may expose server internals or enable persistent backdoor-like access through server components.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Debugger Evasion
exploitedBy.relevance: Debug endpoints in production can be leveraged by attackers who are aware of debugging interfaces to inspect or manipulate application state.
